analysis.title: What's the Most You've Ever Lost on a Coin-Toss? Getting Closer, but No Fat Pitch Yet
key_insights: SPX is nearing its 200 DMA after correlated selling last week. SOXX is about 40% off its highs. NYSE saw its first 80% downside volume day in nearly a year.

BTIG says these are necessary for a bottom but not a 'fat pitch'. When an 80% downside day is the first in at least three months and SOX closes below its 200 DMA for the first time in at least three months, 20-50 day forward returns are a coin-toss.
Odds of another 80% NYSE downside volume day in the next 30 days are about 73% based on 30 years of data.
A fat-pitch setup likely needs a move closer to 7,000-7,100 on SPX with a bigger breadth washout.
About 58% of SPX names are above their 200 DMA. A more durable bottom typically sees under 30%, as in April 2025.
20-day put/call ratios remain well below levels seen at the March and July SPX lows, so sentiment is not extreme.
Since 1996 there were 15 prior first 80% downside days in at least three months. 11 saw at least one more within 30 trading days, and one-third saw five or more such days.
After those events, average and median SPX returns are negative 5-10 days out. SPX was higher 53% of the time 20 days later, with a +0.31% average return.
SOX closed below its 200 DMA for the first time since May 2025. Similar initial cracks saw some strong bounces, but 50-day returns are negative. BTIG says it is late to press tactical downside.

BTIG thinks SOX needs to retrace to the April breakout point (8k-8300), which would fully retrace the parabolic advance. Purchases from May-October are underwater, creating six months of overhead supply.
QQQ has broken under its 200 DMA and July lows. Next support is the late-2025 and early-2026 highs around $635.
High vs. low quality looks to be bottoming at the 2000 lows after a six-year bear market. This conflicts with the tactical view, since held-up quality names are vulnerable to a near-term unwind.
The MS Quality Short Basket is rolling over below its 200 DMA and support. The Quality Long index is holding support, though another flush toward the 200 DMA would not surprise BTIG.
XLV hit an all-time high Thursday and was nearly 20% above its 200 DMA, the widest spread on record. BTIG calls tactical XLV downside a fat pitch.
AAPL was a beneficiary and hideout during the semi/AI unwind. BTIG thinks it falls in a further risk-off move, or unwinds lower if semis/AI bounce.
BTIG is not a fan of precious metals, but GDX is breaking over a downtrend while spot gold is near YTD lows. Commodity stocks sometimes lead the commodity.
RGLD is a quality set-up, held up better than GDX and gold, and is working back toward recent highs.

tension_points.bull_case: Correlated selling, an 80% downside volume day, SPX near its 200 DMA and SOXX about 40% off highs are necessary ingredients for a bottom, and 20-day returns after similar events turn positive.
tension_points.bear_case: Only 58% of names are above their 200 DMA versus under 30% for a durable bottom, put/calls are not extreme, and another 80% downside day is about 73% likely. It is a coin-toss for 20-50 day returns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A move to 7,000-7,100 on SPX with a bigger breadth washout would set up a fat pitch.
